title: Route each item to the valid or the invalid consumer

blocks.text: A consumer returns nothing: its whole job is a side effect. That makes a pair of consumers a clean way to decouple *deciding* about an item from *what happens* to it.

Write `Router.route(List<String> items, Consumer<String> valid, Consumer<String> invalid)`. Build one dispatcher consumer and run it over `items` with `forEach`. An item is valid when it has visible content; every item goes to exactly one of the two handlers, in list order.
The page's own example list is `["Alice", "", null, "Bob", "  "]`. Make sure every one of those is routed without an exception.

cases.says: Items with text go to the valid handler, in order; empty ones go to the invalid handler.
A string of spaces has no content, so it is invalid too.
A null item is handed to the invalid handler instead of throwing.

concepts: A Consumer takes one value and returns nothing, so its whole purpose is a side effect.
A dispatcher consumer can route each item to one of two consumers, keeping the check apart from the handling.
